briefFull: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Organic Farming – Organic Seed Bank (Ha) is implemented by the Spices Board, India, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India.
details: The Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom: Organic Farming – Organic Seed Bank (Ha) is implemented by the Spices Board, India, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India. The scheme aims to establish organic seed banks in the fields of spice growers for the multiplication of planting materials of indigenous varieties of ginger, turmeric, and other herbal spices with high intrinsic value. It seeks to preserve varietal purity and ensure the availability of quality planting materials for organic spice cultivation. The scheme is being implemented in accordance with the modalities and guidelines approved by the Competent Authority under the Integrated Scheme for Export Promotion & Quality Improvement in Spices and Research and Development of Cardamom during the 15th Finance Commission period (2021–22 to 2025–26).
benefits:
1. 50% of cost of production @ ₹37,500/- per Ha for ginger and turmeric and ₹22,500/- for herbal spices whichever is less under Gen category and 75% of the cost for SC/ST at a maximum of ₹ 56,000 for Ginger and turmeric and ₹ 34,000/- per Ha for herbal spices of indigenous varieties which are selected for organic cultivation.
1. Individual growers of any of Indigenous varieties of spices viz., Cochin ginger of Kerala, Nadia Ginger of NE states, Alleppey finger turmeric of Kerala, Rajapuri turmeric of Maharastra, Lakadong / Megha Turmeric of Meghalaya and herbal spices of Tamil Nadu having holding size from 0.10 ha to 8 ha who are under organic certification are eligible to avail benefits under this component. A grower/group can avail assistance under the scheme for a maximum of 3 years at a maximum of 2 ha./beneficiary.
1. An ICS without suitable land of its own can avail the assistance for establishing a seed bank in its name in a suitable land of a member in the group identified for the purpose, for distribution of seeds among its members on cost price, by entering into an agreement with the farmer identified for the purpose. The agreement can either be a part in the mandatory contract signed by the farmer with ICS for certification or a separate agreement with consent for sparing his/her land for the purpose and releasing the assistance from Spices Board to the ICS.
eligibility:
1.Preference for Sikkim, other NE States and then Kerala, Tamilnadu & Maharashtra and other states
2. Designated Officials will conduct final inspection and recommend the eligible cases.
howToApply:
[Online]
**Registration**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the [ServicesPlus](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/) website.
Step 2: Click on the “[Register” ](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/citizenRegistration.html)option on the homepage.
Step 3: Fill out the registration form by entering Full Name, Email ID, Mobile Number, Password, selecting State, and Captcha.
Step 4: Review all details carefully and submit the registration form.
Step 5: An OTP will be sent to your registered mobile number or email; enter the OTP and click “Verify.”
Step 6: Registration will be completed successfully, and a confirmation message will be displayed or sent via email.
**Login**
Step 1: The applicant should visit the ServicesPlus website and click on [“Login.”](https://serviceonline.gov.in/dbt/loginWindow.do)
Step 2: Enter your Email ID, Password, and Captcha.
Step 3: Select the relevant service/scheme name.
Step 4: Fill in the required details in the application form.
Step 5: Submit the application.
documentsRequired:
a) Land documents of ownership / legal possession
b) Current year land tax paid receipt / Chitta Adangal/NoC for NE
c) Aadhar card
d) Bank pass book first page
e) Details of organic certification / ICS
f)Contract/Agreement with farmer and ICS, if ICS is setting up the seed bank in farmers field.

faqs.q: What is the objective of the Organic Seed Bank scheme?
faqs.a: The scheme aims to establish organic seed banks in the fields of spice growers for the multiplication of planting materials of indigenous varieties of ginger, turmeric, and herbal spices. It seeks to preserve varietal purity and ensure the availability of quality planting materials for organic spice cultivation.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for assistance under this scheme?
faqs.a: Individual spice growers cultivating eligible indigenous varieties of spices and having land holdings ranging from 0.10 hectare to 8 hectares under organic certification are eligible to apply for assistance under the scheme.

faqs.q: What financial assistance is available for ginger and turmeric seed banks?
faqs.a: General category beneficiaries can receive assistance of up to 50% of the production cost, subject to a maximum of ₹37,500 per hectare. SC/ST beneficiaries can receive up to 75% of the production cost, subject to a maximum of ₹56,000 per hectare.

faqs.q: What assistance is available for herbal spice seed banks?
faqs.a: For herbal spices, General category beneficiaries can receive assistance of up to 50% of the production cost, subject to a maximum of ₹22,500 per hectare. SC/ST beneficiaries can receive assistance of up to 75% of the production cost, subject to a maximum of ₹34,000 per hectare.

faqs.q: Is organic certification mandatory for availing the benefits?
faqs.a: Yes. Only growers who are under a valid organic certification system are eligible to receive assistance under this component of the scheme.

faqs.q: What is the maximum area eligible for assistance?
faqs.a: A beneficiary can avail assistance for a maximum area of 2 hectares under the scheme.

faqs.q: For how many years can a beneficiary receive assistance?
faqs.a: A grower or group can avail assistance under this component for a maximum period of three years, subject to compliance with the scheme guidelines.

faqs.q: Which regions are given priority under the scheme?
faqs.a: Preference is given to beneficiaries from Sikkim and other North-Eastern States. Thereafter, priority is extended to Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, and other spice-growing states.

faqs.q: Is inspection of the seed bank mandatory?
faqs.a: Yes. Designated officials conduct a final inspection of the seed bank and recommend eligible cases before assistance is sanctioned.
